# Quarterly operations report — May–July 2026

## Summary

The quarter closed at €1,233,225 in revenue against €467,640 in costs, for a net
result of €765,585 and a 62.1% margin. The quarter splits into two halves: May and
June grew steadily — June revenue was up 4.6% on May — before July fell back 9.6%
to €389,640, the lowest month of the quarter. Costs stayed flat through the period
(€151,120 rising to €158,240 in June and €158,280 in July), so the July revenue dip
flowed almost entirely to the bottom line. Customer momentum softened on both ends
of the funnel: signings declined each month (86, 74, 63) while churn nearly doubled
(17, 22, 31), cutting monthly net adds from 69 in May to 32 in July. Support held
steady throughout, closing 95.5% of the 1,001 tickets opened over the quarter.

## Key figures

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Quarterly revenue | €1,233,225 |
| Quarterly costs | €467,640 |
| Net | €765,585 |
| Margin | 62.1% |
| Net customer adds | 153 |
| Ticket close rate | 95.5% |
| June revenue growth | 4.6% |
| July revenue growth | -9.6% |

## Notes

- **June cost total doesn't reconcile.** The June report's stated total (€158,240)
  is €300 below the sum of its own cost lines (€158,540). May and July tie out
  exactly. This report uses the published totals; if the line items are correct,
  quarterly costs are €467,940 and net is €765,285 (margin unchanged at 62.1%).
  Worth a correction from whoever owns the June numbers.
- **July revenue reversal.** The -9.6% July decline wiped out June's 4.6% gain and
  then some; July was the weakest revenue month of the quarter while costs held
  flat, so the margin compressed accordingly.
- **Churn is trending the wrong way.** Churned customers rose 17 → 22 → 31 across
  the quarter. Combined with falling signings, net adds dropped by more than half
  from May (69) to July (32).
- **Cloud spend keeps climbing.** Cloud costs rose every month (€21,310 → €23,940
  → €24,760, up ~16% over the quarter) even as July revenue fell — worth a look
  before the pattern carries into Q3.
